properties.areaDesc: South Slopes of the Western Brooks Range; Noatak Valley
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT until October 29 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Mostly rain is expected below 800 feet. The
heaviest precipitation is expected Tuesday and Wednesday. Some rain
is possible near Red Dog Mine Tuesday. The heaviest snow is
expected Wednesday. Temperatures cool Wednesday into Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 10:02AM CDT until October 27 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge affecting
Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, after which the
flood plain between the levees begins to flood.  No damage is
expected. At 15.5 feet, the river reaches minor flood stage, and
flooding between the levees occurs.  No damage to structures is
expected. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage,
inundating the plain between the levees.  Erosion of the levees is
likely.  Water may seep through the levees, flooding adjacent
farmland. At 22.9 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.  While
water remains between the levees at Presidio, areas downstream may
experience significant flooding.  FM 170 downstream of Presidio
will flood in low spots.  Farmland along the river will be
inundated. At 25.0 feet, the river remains between the levees at
Presidio, although continued flows at this level could cause damage
to the levees.  FM 170 downstream will likely be flooded and
impassable in spots.  Farmland around the river will continue to
inundate. At 25.8 feet, the river reaches record stage for the
period of record (1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but
the exact stage is unknown.  FM 170 will be flooded downstream of
Presidio.  Farmland around the river will remain inundated. At 28.2
feet, the river reaches record stage for the period of record
(1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but the exact stage is
unknown.  FM 170 remains flooded downstream of Presidio.  Farmland
adjacent to the river remains inundated. At 30.0 feet, The top of
the levee is reached, and water will begin to overtop the levees.
Major flooding of Presidio and surrounding farmland is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM CDT Monday was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
this morning and continue falling to 4.1 feet (1.2 meters)
Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet (4.7 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet (8.6 meters) on 09/16/2008.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 300 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 27 at 7:02AM AKDT until October 27 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Slick
roads due to black ice.

* WHERE...Anchorage.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT today.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility. Below
freezing temperatures may lead to frost on bridges and roadways.
properties.instruction:
A dense fog advisory means visibilities will frequently be reduced to
less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: Converse County Lower Elevations; North Snowy Range Foothills
properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued October 27 at 8:45AM MDT until October 27 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
possible. Wind gusts between 50 to 55 mph are more likely.

* WHERE...North Snowy Range Foothills including Arlington and Elk
Mountain along Interstate 80, and Converse County Lower Elevations.

* WHEN...Until noon MDT today.

* IMPACTS...Mainly to transportation. Strong cross winds will be
hazardous to light weight or high profile vehicles, including
campers and tractor trailers.
properties.instruction:
A High Wind Watch means there is the potential for a hazardous high
wind event. Sustained wind speeds of at least 40 MPH or gusts of 58
MPH or stronger may occur. Continue to monitor the latest forecasts.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 6:19AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
have caused portions of that snowfall to melt creating many slushy
areas of melting snow and pooling water. Overnight low
temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning are expected to
fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will allow much of this
slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very likely Wednesday
morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles freeze. Areas of
heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the slush a sturdier,
more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted, especially during
the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.
